heraclite-f1.text: Heraclite fleas, misero sic convenit aevo, / Nil nisi turpe vides, nil nisi triste vides. / Ride etiam, quantumque lubet, Democrite ride / Non nisi vana vides, non nisi stulta vides. / In fletu, hic risu modo gaudeat, unus utrique / Sit licet usque labor, sit licet usque dolor. / Nunc opus est (nam totus eheu jam desipit orbis) / Mille Heraclitis, milleque Democritis. / Nunc opus est (tanta est insania) transeat omnis / Mundus in Anticyras, gramen in Helleborum.

translations.literal: Heraclitus, may you weep, thus it befits the wretched age, / you see nothing unless base, nothing unless sad. / Laugh also, and as much as it pleases, Democritus, laugh: / you see not unless vain things, not unless foolish things. / In weeping, this one in laughter let him only rejoice; one for both / may be ever labour, may be ever grief. / Now there is need (for the whole world, alas, now is foolish) / of a thousand Heraclituses and a thousand Democrituses. / Now there is need (so great is the madness) that the whole / world pass into Anticyras, the grass into hellebore.
translations.note: Line 5 reads 'In fletu, hic risu', which leaves 'In' with no clear sense. It probably stands for something like 'Ille fletu, hic risu' ('that one in weeping, this one in laughter'), and the translation follows that reading. In 'unus utrique sit licet usque labor' the word licet ('granted', 'let there be') makes the toil and the grief the same for both men. Anticyra was the town famous for hellebore, the classical cure for madness, so the last line wishes the whole world turned into a madhouse and its grass into medicine.
translations.text: Weep, Heraclitus, for so it suits this wretched age: / you see nothing but what is base, nothing but what is sad. / Laugh too, Democritus, laugh as much as you please: / you see nothing but what is vain, nothing but what is foolish. / Let the one rejoice in weeping, this one in laughter; for both alike / let there be the same unending labour, the same unending grief. / Now there is need (for alas, the whole world now plays the fool) / of a thousand Heraclituses and a thousand Democrituses. / Now there is need (so great is the madness) that the whole / world be turned into Anticyras, and its grass into hellebore.
